mission_06: Quantum advantage in ML arises when quantum systems can represent or process information more efficiently than classical systems. Key indicators include: entanglement entropy (high entropy means the state cannot be efficiently represented classically), Schmidt rank (high rank indicates complex correlations), and state complexity (the classical memory needed to represent the quantum state). The von Neumann entropy of a subsystem's reduced density matrix measures entanglement: S = -Tr(rho log rho). A maximally entangled n-qubit state has entropy n/2 bits. In this mission, you implement entanglement entropy computation via partial trace, state complexity analysis including Schmidt rank decomposition, and a quantum advantage analyzer that evaluates whether a dataset's quantum encoding creates sufficiently entangled states to potentially outperform classical methods.
